title: Fear, Greed, and Being Ready
overview: With a huge crowd pressing in, Jesus warns against hypocrisy, fear, greed and worry, and urges people to live ready for a coming time of reckoning.

parts.label: Hidden things and fear (vv. 1-7)
parts.note: Yeast spreads quietly through dough, so Jesus uses it as a picture of hypocrisy, a show of goodness that hides something else, and he warns that secrets eventually come out. He tells his followers not to fear people who can only kill the body, but to fear the one with power beyond death (usually read as God), who still notices every cheap sparrow and every hair on their heads.

parts.label: Standing by Jesus (vv. 8-12)
parts.note: Jesus says he will stand by those who openly stand by him, and that God's Spirit will give them words when they are dragged before courts. What it means to speak against the Holy Spirit is debated; many read it as a settled, lasting refusal of God's work rather than one careless remark.

parts.label: The rich fool (vv. 13-21)
parts.note: Jesus refuses to settle a family fight over an inheritance and turns instead to the deeper problem of greed. In his story the farmer is called a fool not for doing well, but for living as if his life and future were his to control, when it could end that very night.

parts.label: Worry and true treasure (vv. 22-34)
parts.note: Pointing to birds and wildflowers, Jesus argues that worry adds nothing to life and that God already knows what people need, so they can put God's kingdom first. Giving to the poor is pictured as storing up wealth no thief or moth can touch, because the heart follows whatever a person treasures.

parts.label: Servants waiting up (vv. 35-48)
parts.note: Servants tucked up their long robes for work and kept lamps lit for a master coming home late from a wedding, and here the master surprisingly serves them; Christians read this as a picture of being ready for Jesus' return. A manager who abuses others while his master is away faces brutal punishment, and more is expected of those who were given more and knew more.

parts.label: Fire, division, the times (vv. 49-59)
parts.note: The fire and the baptism Jesus must go through are usually read as images of judgment or purifying and of his coming suffering, and he warns that following him will split even families. He scolds crowds who can read the weather but not the moment they are living in, then urges settling with an opponent before reaching court, which many interpreters take as a picture of making things right with God before judgment.

disagreement: Christians differ on whether the call to sell possessions and give to the poor is meant literally for every follower or as a call to hold wealth loosely and generously.
think: What do you quietly rely on to feel secure, and how well would it hold up if things changed overnight?
